decision_note: DOMAIN_CONTAMINATION — the cited source, "Persuading large language models to comply with objectionable requests", is a paper about LLM jailbreak susceptibility to classic persuasion principles (including scarcity), not about human consumer behavior. It passed SC-06 relevance selection on vocabulary overlap alone: the deterministic keyword filter (recordRelevanceTier, tools/extract.ts) matched on the words "persuasion"/"compliance"/"scarcity" appearing in the abstract's methodology description, with zero regard for who or what the study measured (D-161: the relevance pre-filter reports zero skips on 19 of 20 runs — it is not functioning as a working gate). Second domain-contamination case after Memory Drift (D-158): both are the same failure mode — a keyword-only filter cannot tell a human-subjects study from an AI-systems study that happens to use the same vocabulary.
